plain.headline: God Builds a House
plain.intro: King David wants to build a house for God, but God promises instead to build David a house, a family line whose kingdom will last forever. In the Gospel, the angel Gabriel tells Mary that her son will receive the throne of David and reign without end. Between them, Paul praises God for a plan kept secret for ages and now revealed in Jesus Christ.
plain.listen: the promise God makes to David, and how the angel repeats it to Mary

Reading 1.box: David is now king and lives in a fine palace, and he wants to build a temple for the Ark of the Covenant. God answers through the prophet Nathan with a play on words: David will not build God a house, but God will make David a house, meaning a royal family that lasts forever. The promise first pointed to David's son Solomon, and the Church hears its full meaning in Jesus, the Son of David.

chunks.text: King David was settled in his palace, and the Lord had given him peace from all the enemies around him. The king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I live in a house made of cedar, but God's Ark stays in a tent." Nathan told the king, "Go ahead and do whatever you have in mind, because the Lord is with you."

But that same night, the Lord spoke to Nathan. He told him to go to David and say: "The Lord asks, should you be the one to build me a house to live in? The Lord of hosts says, I took you from the pasture, where you followed the sheep, and made you leader of my people Israel.

I have been with you wherever you went, and I have cleared all your enemies from your path. I will make your name great, like the names of the greatest people on earth. I will give my people Israel a place of their own and plant them there, so they can live in their own land and never be uprooted again. Wicked people will no longer oppress them as they did before, from the days when I put judges over my people. I will give you rest from all your enemies. And the Lord tells you this: the Lord will make you a house.

When your life is over and you rest with your ancestors, I will raise up one of your own children after you, and I will make his kingdom strong. I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. If he does wrong, I will discipline him as people discipline their children. Your house and your kingdom will stand firm forever before you. Your throne will last forever."

Responsorial Psalm.box: The psalm sings of God's faithful love, which stands firm forever. It recalls God's sworn promise to David that his family and his throne would last through every generation.

Reading 2.box: This prayer of praise comes from Paul's letter to the Christians in Rome. God's plan, hidden through long ages and announced by the prophets, has now been revealed in Jesus Christ so that people of every nation may believe and obey.

chunks.text: Glory to God, who is able to make you strong in faith, according to the Good News I preach about Jesus Christ. That Good News reveals the mystery that was kept secret for long ages but is now made known. Through the writings of the prophets, and by the command of the eternal God, it has been shared with all nations so they may come to believe and obey. To the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, be glory forever. Amen.

Gospel.box: The angel Gabriel comes to Mary, a young woman of Nazareth engaged to Joseph, who belongs to the family of David. Gabriel announces that she will conceive by the power of the Holy Spirit and bear the Son of God, who will reign on David's throne forever. The Church calls this scene the Annunciation. Mary's answer, "let it be done to me according to your word," is her yes to God's plan.

chunks.text: In the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin engaged to a man named Joseph, from the family of David. The virgin's name was Mary. The angel came to her and said, "Rejoice, you who are full of God's favor. The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women."

Mary was deeply troubled by his words and wondered what this greeting could mean. The angel said to her, "Do not be afraid, Mary. God is pleased with you. You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus.

He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David. He will rule over the people of Jacob forever, and his kingdom will never end." Mary asked the angel, "How can this be, since I am a virgin?"

The angel answered, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will cover you like a shadow. So the holy child born of you will be called the Son of God. Your relative Elizabeth, whom people called unable to have children, has also conceived a son in her old age, and she is now in her sixth month. Nothing God says is impossible." Mary said, "I am the servant of the Lord. Let it be done to me as you have said." Then the angel left her.

plain.carry: This week I will make room for God's plans, even when they are not my own, and try to answer him as Mary did.

kids.headline: Mary Says Yes
kids.intro: Christmas is almost here. Today we hear about a promise God made to King David long ago, and how God kept that promise when an angel visited Mary.
kids.listen: what the angel tells Mary, and what Mary says back

Reading 1.box: King David wanted to build a beautiful house for God. But God said he would build David a house instead, which meant a family of kings that would last forever. Jesus was born into David's family.

chunks.text: King David lived in a fine palace, and there was peace in the land. He said to the prophet Nathan, "I live in a house made of cedar wood, but God's Ark is kept in a tent." Nathan said, "Go ahead. God is with you." But that night God spoke to Nathan.

God said, "Tell David: Are you going to build a house for me? I took you from taking care of sheep and made you leader of my people. I have been with you everywhere you went. I will make your name great. I will give my people a safe home where no one will hurt them anymore.

I will give you rest from your enemies. And I, the Lord, will build you a house, a family that lasts. After you die, one of your children will be king. I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he does wrong, I will correct him. Your family and your kingdom will last forever."

Responsorial Psalm.box: This song says God's love lasts forever. God promised David that someone from his family would always be king.

Reading 2.box: Saint Paul praises God for a wonderful secret plan. For a long time it was hidden, but now God has shown it to everyone through Jesus.

chunks.text: Praise God, who can make your faith strong. God had a secret plan that was hidden for a very long time. Now God has shown it to the whole world through Jesus, so that everyone can believe in him. Glory to God forever, through Jesus Christ. Amen.

Gospel.box: God sent the angel Gabriel to a young woman named Mary. Gabriel told her she would be the mother of Jesus, God's Son. Mary said yes to God.

chunks.text: God sent the angel Gabriel to a town called Nazareth. He went to a young woman named Mary, who was a virgin and was going to marry a man named Joseph, from King David's family. The angel said, "Rejoice, Mary, you are full of God's blessing. The Lord is with you."

Mary was surprised and wondered what this meant. The angel said, "Don't be afraid, Mary. God is pleased with you. You will have a baby boy, and you will name him Jesus. He will be called the Son of the Most High God. He will be king like his ancestor David, and his kingdom will never end."

Mary asked, "How can this happen, since I am a virgin?" The angel said, "The Holy Spirit will come to you, and God's power will cover you. So your child will be holy, the Son of God. Your relative Elizabeth is going to have a baby too, even though she is old. Nothing is impossible for God." Mary said, "I am God's servant. Let it happen as you said." Then the angel left.

word.meaning: An angel is a spirit made by God who serves him and sometimes brings his messages to people.

kids.draw: Draw the angel Gabriel visiting Mary, and write Mary's answer, "Let it happen as you said," at the bottom.
kids.ask: Mary said yes to God even though she was surprised. What is one way you can say yes to God this week?

family.opener: Today we hear how God kept a very old promise to King David, through a young woman named Mary who said yes.
questions: David wanted to give God a house, but God gave David a gift instead. When has God surprised us with something better than we planned?
Mary was troubled and asked a question, and then she said yes. What helps us trust God when we do not understand?
How can our family make room for Jesus in these last days before Christmas?
family.try: Each day this week, have everyone choose one helpful job at home and do it without being asked, as a way of saying yes to God like Mary.
family.pray: Faithful God, you keep every promise, so help our family say yes to you as Mary did and welcome Jesus with open hearts.
